div.div:
The tag byte packs two things:
0x2a = 0b00101 010
upper bits 00101 = field number 5 (name)
lower 3 bits 010 = wire type 2 (length-delimited: string, bytes or nested message)
So the field's name never goes on the wire, only its number. That is why the receiver needs the same schema.

div.div:
The length is a varint: small numbers take 1 byte, numbers up to 16383 take 2, and so on. 25 fits in one byte.
Timestamps use a different trick: fixed64, always 8 bytes, because a nanosecond epoch time is so large a varint would need 9.

div.div: Overhead for this field: 2 bytes on 25 bytes of content. Protobuf is cheap per field. The span is big because of what is in it, not how it is encoded.
